param_input_item.param_description: selects nelson-cli when passed to the nelson launcher.
selects nelson-adv-cli when passed to the nelson launcher.
selects nelson-gui when passed to the nelson launcher.

selects nelson-webview in desktop webview mode when passed to the nelson launcher. Passed directly to nelson-adv-cli it is instead an option that renders figures with the web (RenderWeb) backend, with no Qt figure windows, while keeping the terminal REPL.
selects nelson-webview in HTTP server mode when passed to the nelson launcher. The same option selects server mode for the direct nelson-webview executable.
sets the HTTP host. This option is valid only with --web, --webview, or the direct nelson-webview executable.
sets the web port from 1 to 65535. This option is valid only with --web, --webview, or the direct nelson-webview executable.
stops Nelson option parsing. Arguments after this separator are returned by argv('user').
executes a Nelson command after startup. Options -e and -f are mutually exclusive.
executes a Nelson script file after startup. Options -e and -f are mutually exclusive.
executes a Nelson script file in an existing Nelson process or creates one. GUI mode only.
displays help about program options.
returns Nelson version.
enables Visual Studio Code mode.
opens one or more valid existing files in the text editor. GUI mode only.
loads one or more valid existing .nh5 or .mat files.
disables the main Nelson startup script.
disables loading user modules.
disables the user startup script.
minimizes the main window. GUI mode only.
disables interprocess features.
disables file watcher features for this session.
disables audio module startup code.
disables python_engine module startup code.
sets the session language. Currently, lang can be: fr_FR en_US.
starts without displaying the banner and version.

description.p: nelson-cli: basic terminal, no gui framework dependency, no history, no completion.
nelson-adv-cli: advanced terminal, no graphical console, history and completion available.
nelson-gui: graphical console, history and completion available.

nelson --webview and nelson-webview open a native desktop webview by default with a private localhost port that is not printed. Supplying --url or --port keeps the webview open and publishes the same session at the selected HTTP address. If the native webview is unavailable, Nelson stops with an error.
nelson --web and nelson-webview --web start an HTTP server without opening a desktop window and print the served URL.

Mode selector options --cli, --adv-cli, --gui, --webview and launcher-level --web are only valid for the generic nelson launcher. Direct executables such as nelson-cli, nelson-adv-cli and nelson-gui reject them before --. The single exception is nelson-adv-cli --webview, where --webview is accepted as an option that switches the figure backend to web (RenderWeb) rendering.
After --, mode selector tokens are normal user arguments and can be read with argv('user').
Module startup arguments such as --no-audio and --without-python remain visible in argv() for compatibility. New command builders should place user arguments after -- and read them with argv('user').
Quotes used to group arguments are interpreted by the operating system or shell before Nelson starts. Use a portable form such as nelson-cli -e "disp('hello world'); quit".
If Nelson is installed on Windows, the NELSON_RUNTIME_PATH environment variable is defined and can be used to call "%NELSON_RUNTIME_PATH%\nelson.bat".

history_item.history_description: command line options standardized: mode selectors now use the double dash form (--cli, --adv-cli, --gui) and multi-word options use kebab-case (--no-startup, --no-user-startup, --no-user-modules, --no-ipc, --no-audio, --without-file-watcher, --without-python, --without-julia)
